patient.chief_complaint: Wife called 911 - husband confused and not responding appropriately for 45 minutes, brief shaking earlier
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Davis is a 65-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes but no known epilepsy who presents with altered mental status. His wife reports that he was watching television when he had a brief episode of shaking lasting about 30 seconds approximately 45 minutes ago. He did not fall. After the shaking he seemed confused and has remained confused since — he is saying nonsensical things and is disoriented. She thought he would recover but he has been persistently confused for 45 minutes. He has never had a seizure before. She denies any headache, fever, or focal weakness preceding the episode. He has had no recent illnesses. He was at his baseline this morning. He has no substance use except moderate alcohol. His blood glucose at home was 84 mg/dL when she checked it during the episode, ruling out hypoglycemia. On arrival he is awake but confused and disoriented, unable to follow complex commands. EEG was immediately performed as the presentation suggested possible non-convulsive status epilepticus. The clinical presentation of persistent confusion following a brief convulsive event without recovery is a classic NCSE pattern that can mimic stroke, metabolic encephalopathy, or postictal state.

results.finding: Anti-Hu paraneoplastic limbic encephalitis: strongly associated with SCLC (80% of cases)
Treatment: immunotherapy (IVIG, steroids, plasmapheresis) + treat underlying cancer
Anti-Hu: often refractory to immunotherapy alone; treating SCLC is essential
NCSE from paraneoplastic encephalitis: AEDs + immunotherapy + oncology treatment
Prognosis for anti-Hu: poor if SCLC untreated; partial improvement possible with cancer treatment

output.summary: Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) antibody is found in association with paraneoplastic neurological syndromes, most commonly in the setting of small cell lung carcinoma (reported in approximately 75–80% of anti-Hu cases). Limbic encephalitis associated with anti-Hu antibodies is frequently accompanied by electroencephalographic seizure activity. Immunotherapy and tumor-directed therapy have been studied in this population; outcomes vary by extent of underlying malignancy. Clinical correlation required.

useless_tools.rationale: No cardiac source-of-embolus question — MRI ictal-pseudostroke pattern excludes cardioembolic stroke as the mechanism.
No arrhythmia or syncope to evaluate; standard ICU telemetry suffices.
Neuropsych battery cannot be performed in an encephalopathic patient and does not change acute SE management.

sequence_constraints.reason: Head CT must precede LP to exclude space-occupying lesion or hemorrhage that contraindicates LP.
Confirm electrolytes (Ca, Mg, Na) and renal function before loading AEDs to dose appropriately.

critical_actions: Administer IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg as first-line treatment immediately — do NOT delay benzodiazepine for diagnostics
Load second-line AED (levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV, per ESETT) if seizure persists after benzodiazepine
Continuous video-EEG to confirm NCSE control after treatment
Initiate empiric IV acyclovir until HSV PCR returns
Initiate immunotherapy (high-dose methylprednisolone +/- IVIG) once paraneoplastic etiology established
Urgent oncology consultation for tissue diagnosis of suspected SCLC
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT administer IV thrombolysis (tPA) — cortical ribbon DWI is ictal pseudostroke, not vascular-territory infarct
Do NOT defer LP for autoimmune workup after CT excludes mass effect
Do NOT rely on resolution of motor activity to declare SE terminated — continuous EEG is required
key_reasoning_points: Persistent altered mental status after a brief convulsive event in an older patient with no epilepsy is NCSE until EEG proves otherwise
Cortical-ribbon DWI restriction that does not respect arterial territory is the signature of ictal pseudostroke, not acute infarct
Anti-Hu (ANNA-1) positivity is >80% associated with SCLC and demands urgent CT chest / FDG-PET for tumor identification
Intracellular-antigen paraneoplastic syndromes (anti-Hu) are best treated by treating the underlying tumor; immunotherapy alone often disappoints
Salzburg NCSE criteria (rhythmic ≥2.5 Hz with evolution, or LPDs + clinical/EEG response to benzodiazepines) operationalize ambiguous patterns
